title: De cara a: prepararse frente a algo que se aproxima

sections.content: De cara a (with an eye to, facing, in preparation for) frames an action as oriented toward something upcoming or a broader context to keep in mind -- useful for describing institutional goals and structural realities alike. It's followed by a noun phrase or infinitive. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los cuatro países crearon Mercosur, de cara a establecer gradualmente una zona de libre comercio.
items.english: The four countries created Mercosur, with an eye to gradually establishing a free trade zone.

items.spanish: El bloque buscaba avanzar hacia una integración más profunda, de cara a competir mejor en la economía global.
items.english: The bloc sought to move toward deeper integration, with an eye to competing better in the global economy.

items.spanish: Brasil y Argentina, de cara a su propio peso económico, dominaban ampliamente las decisiones del bloque.
items.english: Brazil and Argentina, given their own economic weight, dominated the bloc's decisions by a wide margin.

items.spanish: Mercosur seguiría enfrentando este desafío, de cara al futuro, durante las décadas siguientes.
items.english: Mercosur would keep facing this challenge, looking ahead, over the following decades.

sections.content: De cara a can mean either looking forward to a future goal (de cara a competir mejor) or given/in light of an existing reality (de cara a su propio peso económico) -- context tells you which sense is in play.
